A1.justification: Both complete 17-page PDFs describe SpeeDe3DGS, with matching authors and core pruning/grouping methods. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite substantial rewriting and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, rendering-speed, storage, and training-time results on NeRF-DS, D-NeRF, and HyperNeRF, including component and parameter ablations in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original SpeeDe3DGS experiments and integrations into DeformableGS and 4DGS on MonoDyGauBench, alongside quantitative ablations and qualitative comparisons. Some comparator results are explicitly reproduced from the benchmark manuscript.

M1.justification: The sensitivity score, annealed timestamp perturbation, trajectory grouping, and rigid alignment are retained; ASP is renamed TSS. However, v2 Section 4.2.2 applies group rotations to Gaussian orientations as standard, whereas v1 Appendix A.5.1 explicitly fixes orientations and evaluates rotation modeling only as an alternative.

E1.justification: v2 adds the 50-scene MonoDyGauBench evaluation, introducing four Nerfies scenes and fourteen iPhone scenes and evaluating seventeen HyperNeRF scenes. NeRF-DS and D-NeRF remain, and the eight-scene standalone HyperNeRF experiment already present in v1 is retained rather than newly introduced.

E2.justification: The comparison roster changes substantially. For D-NeRF, v1 Table 2 includes D-NeRF, TiNeuVox-B, K-Planes, HexPlane, FFDNeRF, and SC-GS; these are absent from v2's corresponding benchmark comparison, which adds STG and STG-decoder. EffGS and RTGS match v1's C-D3DGS and 4DGS (ICLR), respectively, and are not new methods merely because their names changed.

E3.justification: Reported defaults change from 80% to 60% densification-stage pruning and from 200 to 2048 motion groups, while retaining 30,000 training iterations. v2 adds the MonoDyGauBench training wrapper and MS-SSIM evaluation, tests TSS on D-NeRF, and changes the principal rendering GPU from A4000 to RTX 3090 and NeRF-DS/D-NeRF training GPU to A5000.

E4.justification: v2 Table 10 expands group-count analysis from unpruned D-NeRF to both NeRF-DS and D-NeRF with and without pruning. It adds TSS comparisons on D-NeRF and HyperNeRF, dataset-specific pruning sensitivity results, and Figure 6 case studies. Conversely, v1's rotation-versus-fixed-orientation and linear-blend-skinning ablations in Table 11 are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three independent runs, including parameter ablations. v2 extends this existing practice to additional experiments without introducing seed reporting, confidence intervals, run-to-run error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds benchmark results in Tables 2–7 and revises existing standalone results. For example, the full NeRF-DS pipeline changes from 23.42 PSNR, 366.73 FPS, and 4.48 MB in v1 Table 1 to 23.66 PSNR, 505.60 FPS, and 21.40 MB in v2 Table 1. These reflect changed configurations and hardware, not controlled performance gains. The separate four-scene HyperNeRF vrig quality results are removed.

T1.justification: The sensitivity approximation, trajectory-distance score, and rigid-alignment objective remain. v2 expands the trajectory definition to include rotations in Equation 8, while removing v1 Appendix A.5.2's linear-blend-skinning deformation and normalized-weight equations. The rotation transformation was already described in v1's appendix; its relocation is not a new derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains acceleration through pruning and shared motion. v2 additionally claims superior image quality to every non-neural baseline while exceeding baseline rendering speeds, whereas v1 principally emphasizes acceleration and compression with quality comparable to its neural baseline. Renaming ASP to TSS does not itself establish a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially develops GroupFlow's interpretation as structural regularization that can improve reconstruction under noisy trajectories, supported by new Nerfies/iPhone discussions. It adds limitations for highly non-rigid regions with too few groups and restricts GroupFlow applicability to explicit-motion frameworks. v1 instead emphasizes inherited De3DGS pose errors and dependence on trajectory quality.

D1.justification: v2 specifies pruning beginning at iteration 6000 and recurring every 3000 iterations, distinguishes standalone and benchmark implementations, and explains comparator-result provenance. It removes v1's explicit dataset-provided COLMAP initialization statement and Lie-algebra parameterization detail. Documentation is imperfect: Appendix A.5 retains A4000 hardware wording that conflicts with Section 5 and the revised table captions.

R1.justification: Research positioning is substantially reorganized around MonoDyGauBench's fidelity–efficiency comparison and five motion-representation families. New references include MonoDyGauBench, STG, FisherRF, POP-GS, and the iPhone dataset work. The earlier static-pruning and grouped-motion foundations remain; renamed methods and publication-metadata updates are not counted as new research.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial method explanations are rewritten. Experiments are reorganized around standalone and benchmark evaluations, and the appendices are extensively reordered. Terminology changes include ASP to TSS and De3DGS to DeformableGS.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column presentation. The teaser is redesigned, existing diagrams and comparison panels are revised, Figure 5 becomes separate dataset-specific grids, and Figure 6 adds qualitative comparisons. Benchmark tables are added, component tables are expanded, and the earlier design-choice ablation table is removed.

improvement.justification: v1 claims applicability beyond De3DGS without testing its components in another backbone; v2 demonstrates integrations into both DeformableGS and 4DGS under a common benchmark, substantially strengthening evidence for transferability and revealing backbone-dependent fidelity losses. Expanded group/pruning interaction analyses further improve support for design tradeoffs. These gains outweigh the lost rotation/LBS ablations, although mixed-GPU training comparisons, inconsistent speedup ratios in Table 1, and conflicting hardware descriptions in Appendix A.5 weaken confidence in exact timing claims.
